Our research demonstrates how probabilistic decision models improve agroecological decision-making by systematically addressing uncertainty and trade-offs. By integrating expert-elicited probabilities into structured frameworks, we enhance the assessment of agroecological interventions, ensuring that decision-support tools reflect real-world constraints and variability.

Spatial models and Bayesian networks further strengthen agroecological assessments by improving land-use classification and mapping of complex agroecosystems. @liman_harou_mapping_2020 and @liman_harou_crop_2021 applied Bayesian networks and remote sensing to develop probabilistic spatial models, offering more accurate classifications of flood-based farming systems and land-use transitions.

Participatory decision-support frameworks have proven essential for enhancing farmer engagement and policy impact. In @luu_stakeholder_2024, we demonstrated how stakeholder-driven agro-climate services improve scalability and adoption, while @do_decision_2020 applied co-created decision models to align agroforestry adoption strategies with smallholder realities. These approaches ensure that decision models remain contextually relevant and actionable.

Expanding multi-criteria decision analysis will further improve trade-off assessments in agroecology, particularly in balancing production, conservation, and socio-economic factors. Strengthening science-policy-practice networks will enhance transdisciplinary collaborations, ensuring that research outputs are effectively translated into actionable policies. Finally, developing hybrid models that integrate expert knowledge with select data-driven approaches will improve decision accuracy and adaptability, supporting scalable and resilient agroecological transitions.
